result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [send_slack_notification()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Create an action that sends a Slack notification about a validation. twitter-card: title: >- [send_slack_notification()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Create an action that sends a Slack notification about a validation. title: >- [send_slack_notification()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Create an action that sends a Slack notification about a validation. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Create an action that sends a Slack notification about a validation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/actions.py#L13-L343){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature send_slack_notification( webhook_url=None, step_msg=None, summary_msg=None, debug=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Slack is a common place for a team to hear about problems with its data. The `send_slack_notification()` function creates an action that posts a message to a Slack channel through an [incoming webhook](https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks). The same action works in two places: 1. In [`Actions`](`pointblank.Actions`), it sends a message about a step that exceeded a threshold level. 2. In [`FinalActions`](`pointblank.FinalActions`), it sends a summary of the whole validation after the interrogation. The action works out from where it runs which kind of message to send. The messages are made from templates (`step_msg=` and `summary_msg=`), which can use Slack's Markdown formatting. A notification that can't be sent (because of a wrong webhook URL, a network error or a template with an unknown variable) doesn't stop the validation. The error is printed as `Failed to send Slack notification: ...` instead of being raised. Without a webhook URL, nothing is sent to Slack, which is useful for trying out templates: - With `webhook_url=None`, the action prints the message that it would send. - With `webhook_url=None` and `debug=True`, the function prints previews of both templates filled in with sample values. It then returns `None` instead of an action. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [webhook_url]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The URL of a Slack incoming webhook (`https://hooks.slack.com/services/...`). Since anyone with the URL can post to the channel, it's best read from an environment variable rather than written in the code. The default is `None`, which prints the messages instead of sending them. [step_msg]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The template for messages about a step, using the variables in *Template Variables for Step Messages* below. The default is `None`, which uses a template with the assertion type, the threshold level, the step number, the column and the time. [summary_msg]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The template for summary messages, using the variables in *Template Variables for Summary Messages* below. The default is `None`, which uses a template with the highest threshold level reached, the number of steps, the number of failing steps and the time. [debug]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to print each message, and Slack's response, when it's sent. With `webhook_url=None`, the function prints previews of the templates instead (see above). The default is `False`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Callable or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The action, to use in `Actions` or `FinalActions`. With `webhook_url=None` and `debug=True`, the function returns `None` after printing the previews. ::: ## Template Variables For Step Messages {.doc-template-variables-for-step-messages} A `step_msg=` template can use these variables: - `"{step}"`: The step number. - `"{column}"`: The column name. - `"{value}"`: The value being compared (only available in certain validation steps). - `"{type}"`: The assertion type (e.g., `"col_vals_gt"`, etc.). - `"{level}"`: The threshold level (`"warning"`, `"error"`, or `"critical"`). - `"{level_num}"`: The threshold level as a number (`30`, `40`, or `50`). - `"{autobrief}"`: A localized and brief statement of the expectation for the step. - `"{failure_text}"`: Localized text that explains how the validation step failed. - `"{time}"`: The time of the notification. These are the keys of [`get_action_metadata()`](`pointblank.get_action_metadata`)'s dictionary, plus `"{time}"`. ## Template Variables For Summary Messages {.doc-template-variables-for-summary-messages} A `summary_msg=` template can use these variables: - `"{n_steps}"`: The total number of validation steps. - `"{n_passing_steps}"`: The number of validation steps where all test units passed. - `"{n_failing_steps}"`: The number of validation steps that had some failing test units. - `"{n_warning_steps}"`: The number of steps that exceeded a 'warning' threshold. - `"{n_error_steps}"`: The number of steps that exceeded an 'error' threshold. - `"{n_critical_steps}"`: The number of steps that exceeded a 'critical' threshold. - `"{all_passed}"`: Whether or not every validation step had no failing test units. - `"{highest_severity}"`: The highest threshold level reached in the validation: `"warning"`, `"error"` or `"critical"`. If no threshold was exceeded, it is `"some failing"` when some test units failed and `"all passed"` otherwise. - `"{tbl_row_count}"`: The number of rows in the target table. - `"{tbl_column_count}"`: The number of columns in the target table. - `"{tbl_name}"`: The name of the target table (`"Unknown"` without a `tbl_name=`). - `"{validation_duration}"`: The duration of the validation in seconds. - `"{time}"`: The time of the notification. These are keys of [`get_validation_summary()`](`pointblank.get_validation_summary`)'s dictionary, plus `"{time}"`. Its other keys, such as `"{overall_health_score}"` and `"{list_failing_steps}"`, can be used too. Since the templates are filled in with Python's `str.format()`, a literal brace has to be doubled (`"{{"` or `"}}"`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's validate a small table of orders, which has a missing customer name and two amounts that aren't positive. The action has no webhook URL, so it prints the message instead of sending it. In `Actions(critical=)`, it runs for the steps that exceed the critical threshold: ::: {#0002a669 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl orders = pl.DataFrame( { "amount": [29.99, 150.00, -5.00, 75.50, 0.00], "customer": ["Alice", "Bob", None, "Dana", "Eve"], } ) notify_slack = pb.send_slack_notification() validation = ( pb.Validate( data=orders, tbl_name="orders", thresholds=(0.05, 0.20, 0.40), actions=pb.Actions(critical=notify_slack), ) .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer") .col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0) .interrogate() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` === Dry Run === Would send to Slack: *Data Validation Alert* • Type: col_vals_gt • Level: critical • Step: 2 • Column: amount • Time: 2026-10-29 12:56:57.021509 ============== ``` ::: ::: Only the second step, with 40% of its test units failing, reached the critical threshold, so there is one message. The first step (20% failing) exceeded the error threshold, which has no action here. In `FinalActions`, the same action sends a summary of the validation instead: ::: {#db699781 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} validation = ( pb.Validate( data=orders, tbl_name="orders", thresholds=(0.05, 0.20, 0.40), final_actions=pb.FinalActions(notify_slack), ) .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer") .col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0) .interrogate() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` === Dry Run === Would send to Slack: *Data Validation Summary* • Highest Severity: critical • Total Steps: 2 • Failed Steps: 2 • Time: 2026-10-29 12:56:57.029036 ============== ``` ::: ::: The summary is sent once per interrogation, whether or not any step failed. Both steps failed here, and the highest threshold level reached was critical. Custom templates can add more detail. With `webhook_url=None` and `debug=True`, the function shows previews of the templates with sample values, without a validation: ::: {#a7f8d46e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} pb.send_slack_notification( step_msg=( "🚨 *Step {step} ({type})* exceeded the {level} threshold\n" "• Column: {column}\n" "• Details: {failure_text}" ), summary_msg=( "📊 *Validation of {tbl_name}*: {highest_severity}\n" "• Failing steps: {n_failing_steps} of {n_steps}\n" "• Rows: {tbl_row_count}" ), debug=True, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` === Step Notification Preview === 🚨 *Step 1 (col_vals_gt)* exceeded the critical threshold • Column: column_name • Details: 25% of values failed this test === Summary Notification Preview === 📊 *Validation of example_table*: critical • Failing steps: 2 of 5 • Rows: 1000 ``` ::: ::: The sample values show where each variable goes. For a real channel, we pass the webhook URL and use the action for both kinds of message. With `Actions(default=)`, a step message is sent for every step that exceeds a threshold, at its highest level: ```python import os notify_slack = pb.send_slack_notification(webhook_url=os.environ["SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"]) validation = ( pb.Validate( data=orders, tbl_name="orders", thresholds=(0.05, 0.20, 0.40), actions=pb.Actions(default=notify_slack), final_actions=pb.FinalActions(notify_slack), ) .col_vals_not_null(columns="customer") .col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0) .interrogate() ) ``` This interrogation posts three messages to the channel: one for each failing step (at the error and critical levels), then the summary. Reading the URL from the `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` environment variable keeps it out of the code. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~Actions`) : Run actions when a step exceeds a threshold level. [](`~FinalActions`) : Run actions after an interrogation. [](`~get_action_metadata`) : Get the information that step messages are made from. [](`~get_validation_summary`) : Get the information that summary messages are made from. [](`~emit_otel`) : Send validation metrics to OpenTelemetry from a final action.
